summary: Research brief for utilityexplained.com's Amazon Associates pivot: 5 verified competitor analyses (EnergySage, ChooseEnergy, SaveOnEnergy, EnergyBot, Wirecutter), Amazon Associates commission rates verified from the official rate table, keyword-demand gaps identified against the live corpus, search-intent monetizability map, E-E-A-T patterns, and a labeled revenue model skeleton. Key finding: the site's single 'product' article (50-best-smart-plugs) contains ZERO affiliate links — the entire monetization plumbing (amazon.html + product-box.html shortcodes) exists but is unused, and hugo.toml carries the wrong tag (litwd-20 vs utexplained-20).
findings: FACT (disk): hugo.toml amazon_tag='litwd-20' but owner's real store ID is 'utexplained-20' — every link built before fixing this attributes earnings to the wrong tag. amazon.html and product-box.html shortcodes both read .Site.Params.amazon_tag with default 'litwd-20', so a single config change fixes all links sitewide.

FACT (disk): content/blog/50-best-smart-plugs-standby-power.md — the only product-adjacent article — contains ZERO amazon.com links and ZERO product-box shortcodes. It is a safety/measurement guide citing DOE sources, with no ASINs. The 'product recommendation' article is not monetized at all.

FACT (web, retrieved 2026-08-27, https://www.nytimes.com/wirecutter/): Wirecutter (NYT) is the E-E-A-T gold standard for product reviews: 'We independently review everything we recommend. We may make money from the links on our site.' — canonical disclosure; staffer bylines, testing methodology, no fabricated testing.

INFERENCE: The utility-bill question space splits into two monetizability tiers. HIGH: 'how to lower electric bill' (site's #1 page, 123 sessions), 'why is my electric bill so high', 'water bill too high', 'time of use', 'heat pump vs gas furnace', 'EV charging impact', 'smart meters' — these carry product intent (smart thermostats, smart plugs, energy monitors, leak detectors, EV chargers, heat pumps). LOW (pure info, the 91%-bounce definitional pages): 'what is CCF', 'how to read gas meter', 'reconnection fee', 'billing cycle', 'stormwater fee', 'sewer charges', 'fuel adjustment charge' — no product intent; these need internal links to monetizable pages or a calculator to convert.

INFERENCE (corpus gap analysis vs live file list): high-volume queries NOT covered: (a) per-state average-bill pages (only 4 state-ish pages exist: average-utility-costs-2026, average-utility-bills-by-state-2026, 2026-utility-cost-index-by-state, 7-states-with-worst-utility-spikes — no 50-state coverage); (b) heat-pump/IRA rebates — has heat-pump-vs-gas-furnace-savings but NO IRA/Inflation Reduction Act rebate or heat-pump tax-credit page; (c) EV charging — has ev-charging-impact-electric-bill but NO EV-charger buying/installation guide or level-2 charger recommendation; (d) water-lease/infrastructure fees — has stormwater-fee, sewer-charges, drought-surcharge but NO water-lease or infrastructure-replacement-fee page; (e) no product pages for energy monitors, leak detectors, or smart thermostats (only the unmonetized smart-plug article).

INFERENCE (E-E-A-T): the site already has the right bones — editorial-policy, methodology, corrections, editorial-team, 5 author pages, affiliate-disclosure — matching the verified competitor patterns (EnergySage/ChooseEnergy editorial-guidelines pages, Wirecutter disclosure line). The compliance risk flagged in the evidence brief stands: author personas are UNVERIFIED, and the site was AdSense-blocked for 'Low value content' — so E-E-A-T remediation is a prerequisite, not an option, before affiliate links can convert.

ASSUMPTION (labeled): Amazon EPC for this niche is not published by Amazon. Industry info-content EPC is typically $0.05–0.15/click; product-review pages $0.20–0.50. Conversion 5–10% of clicks; CTR 3–8% on monetizable pages. AOV: smart thermostat $150–250, smart plug $15–25, leak detector $30–50, energy monitor $50–80. Lead-gen (EnergySage/ChooseEnergy-style) pays $50–500 per qualified lead — far higher than product commission.
